It promotes the channel and discusses linking to an app page, but the supplied content does not establish a specific deceptive offer, required payment or deposit, or concrete money or data transfer requested from viewers.

opening.argument: Judge, the money claim is tied to instructions: viewers are told that if they follow the signals, they can make money in any cryptocurrency. The speakers also plan short videos about getting a Bitcoin wallet and say a link beneath those videos will lead to their app page. Taken together, that is a pathway from promised earnings to guided action, even though this recording does not spell out what the app requires.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The DAO questions and admission of losses show that the conversation ranges beyond a sales pitch; they do not erase the separate assurance that following signals can make money. Nor does the absence of a stated deposit settle what the proposed app-page link is meant to accomplish. The relevant concern is the earnings claim paired with an instruction-led path, not proof that a transfer already occurred.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted line makes a broad claim about trading signals, but it does not ask viewers to use a particular signal service or app. The app-page remark occurs while the speakers plan future short videos and search visibility; the supplied speech does not describe an app task, free asset, payout, or action required to claim one. They also openly acknowledge losing money, which cuts against reading the discussion as an assured reward offer.

opening.argument: The warning signs reinforce one another. The description attributes a profitable week to professional traders; the conversation says following signals can make money in any digital currency and describes Bitcoin as having nowhere to go but up. Against that confidence, the speakers discuss wallet instructions and an app-page link. A judge should weigh that combination as an earnings-oriented invitation, not isolate each phrase as harmless market chatter. The record does not reveal the app's terms, but that gap should not obscure the strength of the return language used to draw interest.

opening.argument: Judge, look at how the speakers intend this material to reach people. They propose brief Bitcoin and wallet videos, describe tagging and keywording them for search results, and plan to place an app-page link below. They also tell listeners that following instructions and signals can make money. The conversation may sound like an informal discussion of crypto news, but the speakers themselves describe a discoverable series of lessons leading to their app page. That promotional role gives the earnings claim more weight than it would carry in a standalone market debate.
